steps.where: Integrations › Cookbooks, then the top bar workspace selector
steps.do: Confirm the Precision Skills card is Ready (you do not install it; the lab runs on Skills). Then create a workspace for the lab with the + in the top bar, so a viewer can be added later.
steps.see: The card lists skills, trigger tests, packages, calibration; the top bar shows the new workspace as active.

steps.do: Author the skill in the wizard. The one-line summary is read by the selector together with the name, tags and trigger phrases; the content is never read by it. The name box turns spaces and underscores into hyphens; names must be kebab-case and must not start with claude or anthropic.
fill: the summary line of the asset file
the body of the asset file, below its front matter
stack trace, signing key, database index, sql migration, latency metrics, unit test
steps.see: Back on the list, Open the skill: the header shows v1 and the Author stage's version history shows version 1 live.

steps.do: Render the skill with all three variables, then with only one. Render Preview substitutes {{ vars }} and badges what it could not resolve.
steps.see: Rendered Output contains Cite [KB-1042] (duplicate-charge refunds) and Audience: non-technical customer, with no unresolved badge. With only audience: 2 unresolved and {{ policy_context }} stays in the output.

steps.do: Check one positive, one negative and one near miss. Trigger testing is deterministic (no model): it returns whether the skill is selected, a score and the reason.
steps.see: T01: selected (auto:...). T07: not selected, excluded:negative_trigger:signing key. T27: selected (auto:summary), a false positive the starter phrases let through.

steps.where: Skills › support-tone-and-citation › Scenario Sets, then Trigger Tests
steps.do: Add twelve cases as scenarios (T01 T07 T28 T14 T15 T23 T27 T29 T31 T32 T34 T35; untick Expected: skill should be selected for the engineering ones) and run them. The runner sends the message alone.
steps.click: Run 12 scenarios, then Save as run
steps.see: 9 regression markers and 3 matches expectation; Saved run SKR-…. Scenarios live in the page and are cleared when you leave it.

steps.do: Tighten the trigger phrases. The detail page's Edit form has a Metadata JSON box; replace the test_triggers block with the one in the asset file (3 positive, 14 negative phrases) and keep the rest. This is metadata, so the version does not change.
steps.see: Saved. and the skill_metadata panel lists kubernetes among the exclusions.

steps.where: Skills › support-tone-and-citation › Trigger Tests, then Runs
steps.do: Open the skill again, add the same twelve scenarios and run them: all twelve match. Save the run, then on Runs pin it as the baseline and compare the older run against it.
steps.see: 12 matches expectation, no regression. The latest run is 100% and gets the Baseline marker; viewing the older run shows Net score -75% and 9 regressions.

steps.do: Queue a calibration. It runs in the background and ends at a candidate you review. On the default simulated stack it needs nothing else; on a real-provider stack (--real-llm) first create the skill's test set (Test Sets, then assets/dataset/skill-eval-cases.jsonl, eight rows) and pick it in the Test set box next to Calibrate, with a note on what should change.
steps.see: Calibration queued — job RFN-…; the run reaches candidate_ready. Simulated stack: the review shows Simulated evaluation — not evidence, 0 evaluation examples, gate passed, and a diff with Refinement added by SkillMetaPrompt. Real provider: no simulated banner, 8 evaluation examples, the test set id, gate passed, and a model-written diff (the gate can also reject a run: it then shows rejected with the reason, so calibrate again).

steps.do: Apply the candidate, then undo it from the version history. Rolling back never rewrites history: it restores the earlier text as a new version.
steps.click: Apply to skill, then Roll back (on version 2)
steps.see: the skill is now version 2; version 2 live. After Roll back and confirm, version 3 is live with the original text.

steps.do: Export the skill as a package, then try to import it back. The package holds SKILL.md and agents/openai.yaml: the instructions, not the tags, category or trigger phrases.
steps.see: Reject: Import failed: ... already exists; choose rename or merge explicitly. Rename: the copy's detail page, with openai_package but no test_triggers in its metadata; T28 is selected on the copy and not on the original.

steps.do: Provoke the failures: a name that is not kebab-case (the page blocks it), a reserved name and a summary with angle brackets (the server refuses), a calibration on a skill with no baseline (it works the same), and a Viewer who tries to Apply (403).
fill: create a user, add it to the workspace with role Viewer
steps.click: Create Skill; Calibrate; Apply to skill (as the viewer)
steps.see: Must be kebab-case with Continue disabled; skill names starting with 'claude' are reserved; summary must not contain XML angle brackets; No saved runs yet and a normal calibration with no baseline; and for the viewer a red alert with the 403 message (missing required scope) and no Applied banner.

steps.do: Archive every skill the lab created.
steps.see: Skill archived. and on the Skills list the card offers Restore.
